subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- September 04, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - September 04, 2026

Dear Community,

We're excited to share the latest updates from the AcreetionOS team. First and foremost, we'd like to thank everyone who has contributed to the project so far. Your support and enthusiasm are what drive us to continue pushing the boundaries of what a Linux distribution should be.

In the past week, we've seen significant progress on various fronts. The community has been actively engaged, with several notable contributions. The bash2bat conversion script has been pushed, and secret detection has been configured in the .gitlab-ci.yml file. These efforts are crucial in ensuring the security and integrity of our codebase.

On the news front, Arch Linux has released its September 2026 ISO, powered by Linux Kernel 7.2. This is a significant update, and we're excited to see the improvements it will bring to our distribution. Additionally, the first Arch Linux ISO powered by Linux Kernel 7.2 is now available for download.

We've also seen some concerning news about the Arch User Repository (AUR) being plagued by Russian spam and profanities. This is a reminder that we must remain vigilant in our efforts to maintain a safe and respectful community. Furthermore, over 400 Arch Linux AUR packages have been hijacked to deploy infostealer and eBPF rootkit malware. We urge everyone to exercise caution when installing packages from the AUR.

In other news, Audacity 4.0 has been released, and we're excited to see the new features and improvements it brings. We'll be keeping an eye on security updates and will notify you of any important changes.

On the development front, cobra3282000 has made several commits, including fixing issues with older NVIDIA drivers and removing disk encryption. These changes will improve the overall user experience and make our distribution more accessible to a wider range of users.

Natalie has also made significant contributions, including configuring secret detection and SAST in the .gitlab-ci.yml file. These efforts will help ensure the security and integrity of our codebase.

We're proud to be a part of the Linux community, and we're committed to creating a distribution that is truly sovereign and free from lock-ins. We're grateful for your support and look forward to continuing to work together to make AcreetionOS the best it can be.

As always, we're here to help and appreciate any feedback or suggestions you may have. Join us on Discord to discuss the latest developments and share your thoughts on how we can improve.

Thank you for being part of the AcreetionOS community!

Best regards,
Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva
Co-Lead Developer, AcreetionOS
